factions.name: The Veridian Keepers
factions.description: Ancient beings of living wood and moss who keep the Verdant Shore, the Shore of the First Cycle. They watch the flesh-folk with wary curiosity, and they remember everything.

items.name: Grohl's salt-cord
items.description: A cord of salt-white hemp, knotted the old Ash-Walker way. It is stiff with salt and smells of the sea, though Grohl has never seen one.

items.name: Glade-light
items.description: A cap from the Whispering Glade that glows the green of shallow sea-water. It hums if you hold it to your ear.

items.name: Moss-crowned antler
items.description: A stag's antler with moss growing in the forks of its tines.

items.name: Skein of web-silk
items.description: Canopy-spider silk wound on a twig. It is stronger than it has any right to be, and sticks to everything except itself.

items.name: Flask of Veridian sap
items.description: Sap the colour of liquid emerald and thicker than honey. Keep it out of any cut: they say you would dream the forest's dreams and not want to wake.

items.name: Greyheart's cold glass
items.description: A sliver of glass with too many edges. It is colder than ice and reflects nothing at all.

items.name: Void-Husk
items.description: A rod of black stone cut to too many faces, pulsing faintly like something asleep. It is cold through the leaves you wrapped it in.

items.name: Salt of the First Shore
items.description: A cake of grey-white salt-crust from the flats. Held close, it hums very faintly, like a Keeper's staff.

items.name: Bundle of treenails
items.description: Pegs of fallen ghost-oak heartwood, each as long as your hand, bound with root-fibre. Driven wet, they swell and hold. Iron on the Shore cannot say as much.

items.name: Brother Wystan's mask
items.description: A pilgrim's mask of silver, gone dull, dented over the mouth. Scratched inside, small and careful: WYSTAN.

items.name: Greyheart's green heart
items.description: A knot of living heartwood the size of a fist, wet and green and faintly warm. If you hold very still, it beats.

documents.title: A Tale from the Bower's Book
documents.text:
From the book on the root-stand by the glade path, which the Keepers read aloud at dusk to whoever sits. One tale, set down in a careful flesh-folk hand under the Keepers' spiral-script:

Once a Keeper found a seed that shone, and was afraid it would be lost, and kept it in her hand. She kept it a hundred years. The seed did not grow, because it was in her hand, and the Keeper did not grow, because her hand was full.

When she opened her hand at last, the seed was only a seed. It had shone because she was holding it.

So we do not keep things, the tale ends. We plant them, or we give them, or we let the river have them. A full hand cannot be held.

Under it, in another hand: Read to the flesh-folk on the ninth night. They laughed at the end. That is allowed.
documents.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Veridian Keepers and their rule against hoarding are CANON (book3 ch.2, 7; world_bible.md); the book and this tale are GAME-ONLY.

documents.title: An Ore-Hunter's Reckoning
documents.text:
A page from the sack of the man against the root wall, in a hand that started neat:

Down the root-stair with a lamp, a pick and a sack. The Keepers said the green ore is the Mother's and not for selling. The Keepers say a lot.

A vein as thick as my arm in the hall of root columns. I filled the sack by the second lamp.

The sack is too heavy to climb with. I'll rest first.

It is cold here, and it should not be. The root is warm everywhere else. The cold is further down, at the bottom, and it is coming up the way I came down.

I'll rest a little longer. The root has my boots. It's kind about it.
documents.canonStatus: PROVISIONAL foreshadowing within CANON: the Root-Mother (book3) and the cold in the root (book3 ch.6-7), shown before their time; the ore-hunter and his page are GAME-ONLY.

documents.title: The Song of the First Cycle
documents.text:
What the Keepers sing to a sapling on its first night, as Willow-Whisper sang it to you:

Before the first leaf, the Mother.
Before the Mother, the sea,
and the sea was salt, and the salt was song,
and the song went up the roots.

Grow slow, little one. Grow green.
The wood remembers all it is given.
Take, and the wood remembers.
Hoard, and the wood remembers.

When the cold comes over the ridge
(and the cold comes, little one,
it came before, it comes again)
stand still. Hold fast. Be wood.

'There is more of it,' she said, 'but the rest is for when you are older.'
documents.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Root-Mother, the First Cycle, trees that remember everything and the Keepers' rule against hoarding the Weave are CANON (book3 ch.2, 7; world_bible.md), and so is the cold that ended the cycle before (book3 ch.6); the song is GAME-ONLY.

documents.title: The Three Notes
documents.text:
Sister Iselle's page, in a small careful hand, under a drawing of three circles with the third left empty:

Whispering Glade, the eleventh day.
The First Note (Earth): low, under hearing. The roots carry it. It does not change from dawn to dusk.
The Second Note (Spirit): higher, in the caps; brightest after dark, when the glade-light wakes. It changes when a creature passes, as if it were counting.
The Third Note: not here. Between the first two is a gap the exact shape of a note, and the glade holds it open, the way you hold a door for someone you expect.

Elder Orym teaches that the Third Note is Silence. I begin to think it is not silence. I think it is someone who has not yet arrived.
documents.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Silent Pilgrims, Elder Orym and the Original Song's three notes, Earth, Spirit and Silence, are CANON (book3 ch.5, world_bible.md); Sister Iselle and her page are GAME-ONLY.

documents.title: A Glass-Ship's Log
documents.text:
Three pages of a ship's log in an oilcloth packet, the ink run but readable:

The Lantern of Caelum, out of Port Caelum, charting north along the western shore. Fourth week.
Coast all forest. No harbour, no smoke. Trees taller than our mainmast three times over. Sounded a cove under a long black ridge: good holding, deep water close in.
Put the boat ashore on grey-white flats. Salt everywhere, in a crust you could walk on. Cut two sacks.
Night. Lights in the forest, green and gold, moving. Nobody slept.
Morning. The two sacks of salt are back on the flats where we cut them, set down neatly. Nobody aboard will say they did it.
Weighed anchor. Captain says we do not come back to this shore. Captain says a great deal.

(Along the margin, in another hand:) I came back.
documents.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: Port Caelum and its glass ships (world_bible.md), the harbour below the ridge and the Salt-Flats (book3 ch.3) are CANON; the Lantern of Caelum and its log are GAME-ONLY.

documents.title: The Shore Remembers
documents.text:
Willow-Whisper's words, as near as you remember them:

'Before the first leaf there was the sea, and before the sea there was a cold that came from nowhere and went back there. The Root-Mother remembers it. That is why she sleeps so deep.

The flesh-folk in the east say the grey is a wound in the Weave, and they are right. But wounds do not have hands, and the cold you brought me had a hand on it.

Something is looking at the Shore. Not with eyes. The way frost looks at a window.

We will hold. We are wood; we are good at holding. But I think one day flesh-folk will come over that ridge in their hundreds, carrying their dead in their hearts, and the Shore will have to choose whether to let them in.

When they come, I hope they ask first. You did.'
documents.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Root-Mother, the cold that unmade the cycle before this one (book3 ch.6-7), the Pale Kings' gaze on the Shore and the survivors who later come over the ridge (book3 ch.1-4) are CANON; Willow-Whisper's words here are GAME-ONLY foreshadowing.

documents.title: What the Root-Mother Dreams
documents.text:
Set down by Sister Iselle of the Archive of Silence, from the lips of Willow-Whisper, Voice of the Wood, who would not call it a song:

She dreams of rain. Not the rain that falls; the rain that is still deciding to. She dreams of every root in the Shore at once, which is why the Shore grows the way it does, and why nothing here knows when to stop.

When the cold got into her root she dreamed of a mirror, and in the mirror the Shore, with no green in it. Thorn-Hand went down to see and did not come up. The roots closed over the stair. We told ourselves she had closed them.

A short flesh-folk went down and salted the cold. She dreams of rain again.

I have asked the Voice what the mirror was. She says the Pale have a king who wears one. She says it the way you would say the name of a disease.
documents.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Root-Mother, the Silent Pilgrims, the Archive of Silence and the King of Mirrors are CANON (Book 3); this page, Thorn-Hand and the dream are GAME-ONLY.

documents.title: Brother Wystan's Last Page
documents.text:
Folded small in the lining of a silver mask, in a hand that grows larger and less careful as it goes:

Below the root-stair. I have lost count of the days; the light of the sap does not change.
Iselle is right that there is a gap where the Third Note should be. She is wrong that it is empty. Something is in it. It is very low and very cold and very patient, and it fits the gap exactly. Too exactly, I think. A key that fits a lock is not always the key.

The note is louder here. I must hear it closer.

The fog is in the lower rooms. It is not unpleasant. It is quiet. It takes things away one at a time, and you do not miss them as they go.

I have scratched my name inside my mask, in case.

(Under that there are no more words: only three circles, the third filled in.)
documents.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: Brother Wystan and his page. The Silent Pilgrims, their silver masks and the Original Song's three notes are CANON (book3 ch.5); the cold note under the Temple is PROVISIONAL foreshadowing of the Pale.

documents.title: The Lantern Count
documents.text:
Cut into a shelf of bark and left on the mossy rock above the glade, in Moss-Lantern's small, even strokes:

The First Cycle: the Root-Mother dreamed, and the dream had light in it, and the light was kept. That is the first lantern.

The cycle before this one ended in cold. The trees remember it in their rings and will show you, if you ask and do not take. That is the second lantern, and it is lit for what was lost.

This cycle: the glade's caps make their own light, and the Keepers borrow it, a little at a time, and give it back at dawn. That is the third lantern, and it is the one your kind never understands. You keep what you take. We give back what we borrow. That is the whole of the difference between us, and it is enough.

There is a cold in the east again. I have begun to make a fourth lantern. I do not yet know what it is for.
documents.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Root-Mother, the First Cycle, the trees that remember and the Keepers' rule against hoarding are CANON (book3 ch.2, 6-7; world_bible.md); Moss-Lantern and her count are GAME-ONLY, the fourth lantern PROVISIONAL foreshadowing.

documents.title: What the Falls Remember
documents.text:
Pressed into the moss at the lip of the falls, a strip of pale bark in Willow-Whisper's spiral-script, which the wood reads out for whoever asks:

The river has run over this lip since the Root-Mother first dreamed water. It remembers every face that looked down from here. Most of them were ours.

I have looked down from here and seen, far off, a line of white that is the sea; and I have seen the sea turn black in a dream, and the air fill with ash, and people come over the ridge with nothing, and ask. I have seen a pine grow where nothing should. I have seen a wall of salt.

I do not know when. The river does not know when. It only knows that it will still be running. I have left this here so that when they come, and climb, and look down, they will know that someone looked first and did not turn them away.

The wood will keep this leaf green. It keeps what is asked of it, and gives it back.
documents.canonStatus: PROVISIONAL foreshadowing within CANON: the Root-Mother, the Verdant Ocean running to the sea, the survivors who crest the Ridge of Long Shadows, the First Seed and the Salt-Wall are CANON (book3 ch.1-4, 7; world_bible.md), shown before their time; Willow-Whisper's leaf is GAME-ONLY.

quests.title: Let the Wood Learn You
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: Willow-Whisper, the Keepers' rule that magic here is shared and not hoarded, trees that remember everything and the forest's song are CANON (book3 ch.1-2); the walk and its three places are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Walk the Shore so the wood can learn you: the pool under Mossveil Falls, the Whispering Glade and the shore of the Mistmere. Take nothing.
quests.offer:
"The trees here remember everything: the wind, the rain, every foot that crosses a root." Willow-Whisper lays a hand flat on the nearest trunk, as if feeling for a heartbeat. "They do not know you yet. A thing that is not known is a stranger, and the wood is not kind to strangers."

"So walk it. Drink at the pool under the falls. Stand in the Whispering Glade until it hums. Go down to the Mistmere and let the mist touch your face. Take nothing. Here the Weave is a breath to be shared, not a tool to be gripped. If you hoard it, the woods will take your voice."
quests.progress: "Walk on. The wood is still deciding what you are."
quests.complete:
Willow-Whisper tilts her head, listening to something you can't hear. "The falls know your weight. The glade knows your breath. The mere says you stood still long enough to be polite." The moss in her hair stirs like a smile. "Good. Now the wood will tell me when you lie."

That night she sings you the song the Keepers sing to their saplings. Some of it you understand.

steps.text: Walk the Shore: the falls, the glade and the mere.

objectives.text: Drink at the pool under Mossveil Falls
objectives.say: You kneel and drink. The water is so cold it rings in your teeth, and it tastes of stone and green things. Behind the roar of the falls, very low, the ridge is humming.
You stand still among the caps. After a while the glade begins to hum, less a sound than a feeling in the soles of your feet, as if the roots were passing word of you from tree to tree.

objectives.text: Let the mist of the Mistmere touch your face
objectives.say: The mist comes off the water and lies against your skin like a cool hand. Somewhere in the reeds a glass-frog clicks, and another answers, and the whole shore clicks, and then stops, all at once, as if satisfied.

quests.title: The Briar Way
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: Oak-Bane and his staff of white salt-wood, the Veridian Temple and the Root-Mother, and the Temple's stair of calcified roots are CANON (book3 ch.2, 7; world_bible.md); the creeping briars on the old way are GAME-ONLY. The Temple is not entered here: canon has it found and entered later.
quests.summary: Find Oak-Bane on the old way to the Veridian Temple, cut back the creeping briars that have closed it, and look on the Temple's root-stair.
quests.offer:
"There is an old way from Rootfast into the deep wood, to the Veridian Temple, where the Root-Mother sleeps." Willow-Whisper's voice drops, as if the name were heavy. "We walked it every season, to sing to her. This season the briars closed over it. Briars creep, flesh-folk. They do not hunt."

"Oak-Bane keeps the deep wood. He will not want your help. Go to him anyway. He is less angry than he sounds, and angrier than he looks."
quests.progress: "Well? Do the briars still move?"
quests.complete: Oak-Bane says nothing for a long time. Then he lowers his staff of white salt-wood until its foot touches the top of the root-stair, and the whole wood seems to lean in to listen. "She is dreaming," he says at last, in a voice like a dry branch cracking. "She dreams of cold."

steps.text: Find Oak-Bane where the old way goes into the deep wood.

objectives.text: Speak with Oak-Bane on the Temple way
objectives.say: "You bring the scent of the Ash with you." Eyes like smouldering amber look you up and down. "Willow sends me flesh-folk to cut briars. Fine. Cut. The briars on the old way move when no wind moves them. They took a fawn yesterday. They have never done that."

steps.text: Cut back the creeping briars on the Briar Way.
Go down to the root-stair of the Veridian Temple.

objectives.text: Look on the root-stair of the Veridian Temple
objectives.say: Roots calcified white as old bone arch over a hollow, and a stair of the same white roots winds down and down into a green glow. Living roots have grown across it, tight as a basket. Through them you feel, more than hear, a slow heartbeat far below. Not yet, the wood seems to say. Not you, and not yet.

quests.title: Grey at the Heart
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Keepers who merge into the bark of the trees (book3 ch.2) and the cold glass of the Pale (the Pale Shadows, geometric shapes of cold glass, book3 ch.8) are CANON images; the Greying, the withered Keepers and Greyheart are GAME-ONLY, and the Pale reaching the Shore this early is PROVISIONAL foreshadowing.
quests.summary: In the Greying, a grove going grey in the north-east under the ridge, lay the withered Keepers to rest and take what is lodged in the heart of Greyheart, the eldest of them. Bring it to Willow-Whisper.
quests.offer:
"She dreams of cold because cold has come." Oak-Bane points his staff north-east, toward the ridge. "A grove there is going grey from the heart out. Three of our kin went to sing the grey out of it. They are still there. They do not sing."

"Greyheart was eldest of them. Now he is what the grey made of him. Lay them down, flesh-folk, so their wood can go back into the soil. And bring Willow whatever is in his heart. I will not touch it."
quests.progress: "Do not hold it out to me. Put it down."
quests.complete: Willow-Whisper will not take it from your hand. She has you lay it on a flat stone, and looks at it for a long time: a sliver of glass with too many edges, colder than ice, that throws back no reflection at all. "This is not the Wasting," she says. "The Wasting is a wound. This is a hand."

steps.text: Lay the withered Keepers of the Greying to rest, and take what is lodged in Greyheart's heart.

objectives.text: The cold glass from Greyheart's heart
objectives.say: In the split heartwood of Greyheart's chest something glints: a sliver of glass with too many edges. It is so cold it burns.

steps.text: Bring the cold glass to Willow-Whisper.

objectives.text: Bring the cold glass to Willow-Whisper
objectives.say: "Do not hold it out to me. Put it down. There."

quests.title: A Fog That Tastes of Lightning
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the unnatural violet-tinged fog that tastes of ozone and unmaking, the Void-Touchers in the mists below the ridge who have forgotten their human names, their Void-Husks and the Pale Shadows are CANON (book3 ch.2-4, 8); Palemist Hollow, the mist-walkers and this first sighting, before the books, are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Go down into Palemist Hollow under the Ridge of Long Shadows, break the mist-walkers and the pale shadows in the fog, and bring Willow-Whisper one of the black rods the walkers carry.
quests.offer:
"There is a hollow under the ridge where the mist lies all day. We have always let it lie. Mist is the Shore breathing." Willow-Whisper's leaves rustle, though there is no wind. "This mist does not breathe. It is cold and dry in a wet wood. It tastes of lightning. And there are people in it, walking, who have forgotten their names."

"Go down into it. If they are what I fear, they carry the cold in their hands. Bring me whatever they carry. And breathe as little of that fog as you can."
quests.progress: "You smell of it. Cold and nothing. Sit by the lanterns a while."
quests.complete:
Willow-Whisper looks at the black rod for a long time, and for the first time since you met her she looks old. "So. The Pale are looking at the Shore." She wraps it in fresh leaves and sets it in a hollow of the tree, and the tree closes over it, bark creeping like a slow tide. "Not yet in strength. They are tasting us. Testing what we are made of."

"You have done more for this wood than any flesh-folk in a hundred of your years. The Shore will remember it. The Shore remembers everything."

steps.text: Go down into the fog in Palemist Hollow, under the ridge.

objectives.say: The fog doesn't roll in; it is simply there, a bank of mist tinged faintly violet, and as you step into it the warm wet air of the Shore turns cold and dry. It tastes of lightning and of nothing at all. At its edge the grass has gone to ash.

steps.text: Break the mist-walkers and the pale shadows, and take a black rod from a mist-walker.

objectives.text: A black rod from a mist-walker
objectives.say: The mist-walker's hand opens and lets go of a rod of black stone, cut to too many faces, faintly pulsing like something asleep.

steps.text: Bring the black rod to Willow-Whisper.

objectives.text: Bring the black rod to Willow-Whisper
objectives.say: "Wrap it. Not in your hand. In leaves. Give it here."

quests.title: The Reeds Go Quiet
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: glass-frogs in the undergrowth are CANON (book3 ch.2); Reed-Song, the Mistmere and the moss-backed boars are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Drive off six moss-backed boars rooting up the reed-beds on the far shore of the Mistmere. They lie up in the reeds.
quests.offer:
"Listen." Reed-Song is a thin, stooped Keeper the colour of wet reeds, and when she stops moving you lose her against the shore. "The near shore sings. The glass-frogs click and answer. Now listen to the far shore." Nothing. "Boars. Moss-backed, fat and bold, rooting up the reed-beds where the frogs lay. They lie up in the reeds, and they do not like to be found."

"Six. Then the far shore will sing again, and so will I."
quests.progress: "Still quiet over there."
quests.complete: Reed-Song lifts her head. Across the water, faintly, a frog clicks. Then another. "There." She sinks back into the reeds, content. "The mere thanks you. It has a short memory but a long voice."

steps.text: Drive off the moss-backed boars in the reeds of the Mistmere's far shore.

quests.title: Antlers for the Carver
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: on the Shore iron rusts to nothing and the wood is worked instead (book3 ch.1, 3); Alder-Knot, the moss-antler stags and the carving are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Bring Alder-Knot five moss-crowned antlers from the stags of the Antler Meadow, north-west of Rootfast.
quests.offer:
Alder-Knot is all elbows and burls, with wood-shavings caught in the moss of his shoulders. "Iron rusts on the Shore. Everything you flesh-folk carry here goes to rust-lace in a season. So I carve." He holds up a knife-handle of pale antler grown round with a ring of living wood. "Antler, bound in heartwood. It lasts."

"The stags in the meadow are too many this year. They strip the saplings to the white. Bring me five antlers, good ones, with moss on the tines. The meadow will thank you, even if the stags don't."
quests.progress: "Moss on the tines. The meadow ones have it."
quests.complete: Alder-Knot sorts the antlers by some measure only he understands, and keeps all five. "Good. Handles, buckles, and one of them a comb for Willow, if she'll take it." A creak that might be a laugh. "Come back when your iron rusts."

steps.text: Take moss-crowned antlers from the stags of the Antler Meadow.

quests.title: Silk for the Lanterns
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: Veridian sap that glows (the bioluminescent sap mortar of book3 ch.4) is CANON; sap-lanterns with spider-silk wicks, Moss-Lantern, the canopy spiders and the Fallen Ghost-Oak are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Gather six skeins of web-silk from the canopy spiders nesting in the Fallen Ghost-Oak, west of Rootfast, for the grove's lantern-wicks.
quests.offer:
Moss-Lantern is round and slow and smells of warm honey. All round her, little lanterns of rind and resin hang from the roots, waiting for dusk. "Sap burns green-gold and gentle, if the wick is right. Spider-silk is the right wick. Nothing else draws it so slow."

"The spiders in the Fallen Ghost-Oak spin the best silk on the Shore, and lately they have grown too many and too bold to ask. Bring me six skeins. Then Rootfast will be lit tonight, and you may sit under the lanterns and eat a sap-cake. Everyone should, once."
quests.progress: "Six skeins. Wound on a twig, if you can. It tangles."
quests.complete: Moss-Lantern twists the silk into wicks with fingers like soft roots, faster than you can follow. By the time she has finished the light is going, and one by one the lanterns of Rootfast come on, green-gold, up and down the great trunks.

steps.text: Take web-silk from the canopy spiders at the Fallen Ghost-Oak.

quests.title: The Three Notes
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Silent Pilgrims, their dyed linen, silver masks and brass listening-tubes, and their search for the Original Song and its three notes (Earth, Spirit, Silence) are CANON (book3 ch.5, world_bible.md); Sister Iselle, the glade-light and her page are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Gather three caps of glade-light in the Whispering Glade for Sister Iselle, a Silent Pilgrim who has been listening there for eleven days.
quests.offer:
The pilgrim wears layered linen the colours of ochre and sand, and a mask of polished silver over her mouth and nose. She lowers a long brass tube from her ear. "Forgive me. I have been listening to this glade for eleven days, and it has sung the same two notes on every one of them."

"The Archive teaches that the Song had three notes before the cycles began: Earth, and Spirit, and a third we have lost. This glade holds the first two. I need to hear them in my hand, not only in my ear. Bring me three caps of glade-light, the ones that glow. Take them gently. They grow back."
quests.progress: "Gently. They grow back, but they remember being picked."
quests.complete: Sister Iselle holds the glowing caps to her brass tube one after another, and you hear it too, faintly: a low hum, and over it a higher one. Then, between them, a silence that sounds as if it is waiting. She writes for a long while. "Two notes. And the shape of where the third should be." She tears out the page and gives it to you. "Keep it. The Archive has enough copies of my handwriting."

steps.text: Gather glade-light from the glowing caps in the Whispering Glade.
Bring the glade-light to Sister Iselle.

objectives.text: Bring the glade-light to Sister Iselle
objectives.say: "Hold them still. There. Do you hear it?"

quests.title: Green Gold
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: Port Caelum's glass ships (world_bible.md), Veridian sap 'the color of liquid emerald and thicker than honey' and the Ghost-Oaks it is tapped from (book3 ch.4), and the quarrel between harvesting the Shore and singing to it (book3 ch.3) are CANON; Ondine Varro and this errand are GAME-ONLY. Taking the sap costs standing with the Keepers.
quests.summary: Draw three flasks of Veridian sap from the spouts in the old Ghost-Oaks east of the Salt-Flats for Ondine Varro of Port Caelum. The Keepers will not like it.
quests.offer:
"House Glass pays for three things: charts, salt, and anything that glows." Ondine Varro taps a chart weighted down with sea-shells. "This sap glows. In Port Caelum they say a drop of it mends a cracked hull of glass so you'd never find the seam. Nobody in Port Caelum has ever seen any."

"There's a stand of old Ghost-Oaks east of the flats, with spouts already cut in them. Somebody taps them. Three flasks, and I'll pay more than a season of honest work." She doesn't smile. "The wood-folk won't thank you. I'm not asking them. I'm asking you."
quests.progress: "Three flasks. Stopper them well. It creeps."
quests.complete: Ondine holds a flask to the light. The sap moves in it slowly, the colour of liquid emerald, and throws green across her face. "Look at that." For a moment she forgets to be a trader. Then she remembers, and counts out more gold than you've seen since the Rim. "House Glass remembers the people it trades with. So, I'd guess, do the trees."

steps.text: Draw Veridian sap from the spouts in the old Ghost-Oaks east of the Salt-Flats.
Bring the sap to Ondine Varro.

objectives.text: Bring the sap to Ondine Varro
objectives.say: "Careful. Don't let it touch your skin."

quests.title: The Old King of the Deep Wood
quests.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY (Old Ninebranch). Oak-Bane, guardian of the deep woods, is CANON (book3 ch.2, world_bible.md).
quests.summary: Put down Old Ninebranch, the great stag of the deep wood west of the Antler Meadow, before the grey in his antlers spreads to the herd. He is very dangerous.
quests.offer:
"Old Ninebranch was a fawn when I was a sapling." Oak-Bane's voice is the creak of a whole tree in a wind. "He has been king of the deep wood longer than your kind has had kings. This spring the grey got into his antlers. Now he gores anything that moves. A Keeper, yesterday. Not badly. He was always very good at it."

"I cannot do it. I have known him too long, and he knows how I move. You, he does not know. Make it clean."
quests.progress: "He beds down on the knoll west of the meadow. He will have heard you coming."
quests.complete: Oak-Bane listens to you tell it, and for once he does not interrupt. "Nine branches. I counted them every spring." He turns away toward the deep wood, where the old king bedded down for longer than anyone remembers. "The Root-Mother will take him back. She takes everything back." A pause. "Go. Before I decide I am angry with you."

steps.text: Put down Old Ninebranch on his knoll in the deep wood.

quests.title: Salt of the First Shore
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Salt-Flats of the western coast (book3 ch.3), the Keepers' staves of white salt-wood (book3 ch.2), Mother Vane and Salt of the First Sea (book1 ch.20) are CANON; that the Ash-Walkers' old salt first came from these flats is GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Break three cakes of salt-crust on the Salt-Flats where the Wending meets the sea, and carry them back over the mountains to Mother Vane on the Ashland Rim.
quests.offer:
"The salt your Ash-Walker came for." Willow-Whisper turns Grohl's knotted cord in her fingers. "The sea left it on the flats long ago, when the world was younger and the sea was taller. We make our staves from the wood that grows in it. Salt-wood. It hums."

"Go to the flats where the Wending meets the sea. Break three cakes of the crust, no more. Carry them back over the mountains to your Salt-Speaker. Tell her the Shore remembers her grandmothers, and that they asked first."
quests.progress: "Three cakes. No more."
quests.complete: Mother Vane breaks a corner off one of the cakes and touches it to her tongue, and her eyes close. "That's it. That's the old salt." When she opens them they are wet, which she will deny. "The wood-folk. Still there. Still keeping it." She sets the cakes on the highest shelf in the cave, where the damp can't reach. "Tell no one in the Rim how far you went for this. They'll want you to go again."

steps.text: Break cakes of salt-crust on the Salt-Flats.
Carry the salt over the mountains to Mother Vane on the Ashland Rim.

objectives.text: Carry the salt to Mother Vane
objectives.say: "From the western shore? The wood-folk's shore?" Mother Vane looks at the salt as if it might bite. "Give it here."

quests.title: The Root-Mother's Deep
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Veridian Temple, the Root-Mother and the Keepers are CANON (Book 3); the deep under the Temple, the cold in the root and the Hollow Root-Warden are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Go down the Temple's root-stair into the Root-Mother's Deep, through the withered Keepers and the mist-walkers that have got in, bring down the Hollow Root-Warden in the Heart, and salt the cold that has lodged in the root.
quests.offer:
"The fog came up out of the ground, not down off the ridge. I know where." Willow-Whisper stands a long time with her hand flat on her own trunk, listening. "Under the Temple. The root-stair the living roots closed. They closed it because something was wrong below, and we did not go and see. We are very old, and very slow, and we did not go and see."

"Go down. The Warden of the roots will not let you pass; he is not himself. Nor are the others. Lay them to rest. And at the bottom, where the Root-Mother dreams, there will be a cold thing in her root. Salt it. Grohl's salt, the First Shore's salt, any salt. Salt remembers what a thing was before."
quests.progress: "Is it done? No. I can hear it still, down in the roots, like a tooth going bad."
quests.complete:
Willow-Whisper lets out a breath that goes on for a long time, and all through Rootfast the lanterns flare green and settle. "She is dreaming of rain again." She looks down at you, and the knots of her eyes are bright. "The Warden was Thorn-Hand. He planted the Guest-Tree. We will grow him a new one."

"When the flesh-folk come over the ridge, and they will, I shall tell them a short one came first, and asked, and went down into the dark for us. Go and sit by the sap-pool. You have earned the warm."

She is quiet a moment. "And then go home, short one. Your elder in Oakhaven has been asking the wind after you. There is a road south-east from your village to the city on the mountain, and two of your young went down it and did not come back. The roots say he means to ask you to follow."

steps.text: Go down the Temple's root-stair into the Root-Mother's Deep.

objectives.text: Go down into the Root Gallery
objectives.say: The stair ends in a hall of roots: columns of living wood from floor to roof, and veins of sap in the walls giving a green light that is not quite enough to see by. The air is warm and smells of earth and something sweet, and under that, faintly, of lightning.

steps.text: Lay the withered Keepers and the mist-walkers in the deep to rest, and bring down the Hollow Root-Warden in the Heart.

objectives.text: Mist-walkers broken in the Sap Well

objectives.say: The Root-Warden goes down slowly, the way a tree does, and lies still. The violet light in his seams goes out, and for a moment, before it is gone, it is green.

steps.text: Salt the cold that has lodged in the root.

objectives.say: You press the salt into the pale root round the black rod. The hoarfrost goes grey, then wet, then is only water on living bark. Far up through the earth something enormous turns over in its sleep, and every sap-vein in the deep brightens at once.

steps.text: Tell Willow-Whisper it is done.

quests.title: Brine-Tusk
quests.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY
quests.summary: An old boar that came up off the salt shore is tearing the south-west wood apart. Reed-Song wants it dead.
quests.offer: Reed-Song sits so still on the bank that the reeds have stopped minding her. "The reed-boars were young and stupid. This one is old and isn't." She points south-west with her chin. "It came up off the salt shore with brine dried white on its tusks. It roots the giants' roots. A tree feels that, you know. Go and stop it."
quests.complete: "Gone?" Reed-Song listens to something you can't hear. "Yes. The wood's stopped flinching." She goes back to watching the water. "Thank you. Mind the salt on your boots; the mere doesn't like it."

steps.text: Kill Old Brine-Tusk in the south-west wood.

objectives.say: The old boar goes down among the roots, and the salt on its tusks crumbles away like frost.

quests.title: Lanterns on the Ridge
quests.canonStatus: CANON place (the Ridge of Long Shadows); GAME-ONLY quest
quests.summary: Moss-Lantern's lantern-post on the ridge road has gone dark. Spiders have come up on the basalt shoulder above Mossveil Falls.
quests.offer: Moss-Lantern turns a lantern in her bark fingers; the moss inside it glows and dims, glows and dims. "I keep a lantern on the ridge road, for the ones who come over the mountains in the dark. It's out. Spiders, on the black stone above the falls: they don't like the light, so they put it out." She sets the lantern down. "Clear the shoulder. Then stand on the ridge and look west, so you know why the light matters."
quests.complete: "You saw it." Moss-Lantern doesn't ask; she can see it on you. "All of it, green to the edge of the world, and one small light at the top of the road so they know where to come down." She hands you a lantern of your own. "Keep it lit."

steps.text: Clear the spiders from the ridge's shoulder above Mossveil Falls.
Stand on the Ridge of Long Shadows and look west.

objectives.say: Below you the Verdant Ocean goes on to the edge of seeing: a thousand greens moving like a tide. Somewhere in it, a lantern's worth of light is all a traveller has to steer by.

quests.title: The Violet Fog
quests.canonStatus: CANON (the violet fog and the Void-Touchers, book3 ch.2-4), shown early: PROVISIONAL
quests.summary: Ondine Varro saw a violet fog below the ridge's south shoulder, and things walking in it. She wants to know what they are, and wants them gone.
quests.offer: Ondine Varro has a glass-ship scout's way of looking past you at the horizon. "Below the ridge, on the south shoulder, there's a fog that isn't fog. Violet. It tastes of the air before lightning." She touches her tongue as if remembering. "Things walk in it. Thin things, that reach. Go at night, when it's thickest, and see them. Then I'd be glad if they stopped walking."
quests.complete: "Void-Touchers." Ondine writes it down in a small hand, then looks at what she has written for a long time. "My grandmother's stories had that word in them. I thought it was a word for children." She closes the book. "Thank you. I'm going to tell the ship to wait a season."

steps.text: Go below the ridge's south shoulder after dark.

objectives.text: Stand in the violet fog at night
objectives.say: The fog is violet and lit from inside. The air tastes of ozone. Shapes walk in it, too thin and too tall, and where one reaches out the moss on the stone goes grey.

steps.text: Put down the Void-Touchers.

quests.title: Briars in the Fern Hollow
quests.canonStatus: CANON Keeper (Oak-Bane); GAME-ONLY quest
quests.summary: Creeping briars have got into the Fern Hollow south of Rootfast. Oak-Bane wants them torn out before they reach the giants.
quests.offer: Oak-Bane's voice is like a branch settling under snow. "The briars that came up the Briar Way have sent runners south. Into the Fern Hollow, where the new ferns glow." He opens a hand like a root unclenching. "They choke what they climb. Go and look at the hollow, and pull them out. Five."
quests.complete: "Five." Oak-Bane is quiet the way a tree is quiet. "The ferns will glow again by the turn of the moon. They always do, if you give them the chance."

steps.text: Look at the Fern Hollow, south of Rootfast.

objectives.say: Ferns the green of new emerald, glowing faintly at their curled tips, and running through them, grey and patient, the briars.

steps.text: Tear out the briars in the Fern Hollow.

quests.title: What the Glade Keeps
quests.canonStatus: CANON places (the Whispering Glade and its mossy outcrop, book3 ch.5) and order (the Silent Pilgrims); GAME-ONLY quest
quests.summary: Sister Iselle asks you to keep the night in the Whispering Glade and carry what you hear to Willow-Whisper.
quests.offer: Sister Iselle does not speak; her order doesn't. She writes on a leaf with a charcoal stick and hands it to you. The Glade speaks after dark. I may not answer it. You may. Listen, and tell the Keeper what it says.
quests.complete: Willow-Whisper hears you out with her eyes closed and her branches very still. "It said that? Then it remembers the Root-Mother before she was sad." She opens her eyes. "Tell the Sister nothing. She will already know. Thank you for carrying it."

steps.text: Keep the night in the Whispering Glade.

objectives.text: Listen in the Whispering Glade at night
objectives.say: The leaves overhead move without wind, and the sound they make is very nearly words: a woman's voice, patient and fond, telling the wood to grow.

steps.text: Tell Willow-Whisper what the Glade said.

quests.title: Rust-Lace
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: on the Shore iron turns to rust-lace in days (book3 ch.3), and Port Caelum's glass ships (world_bible.md) are CANON; Alder-Knot's treenails and this errand are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Take Alder-Knot's bundle of heartwood treenails to Ondine Varro at the scout's camp on the Salt-Flats, whose boat is coming apart as its iron nails rust through.
quests.offer:
Alder-Knot sights down a peg of pale wood as if it were an arrow. "The glass-ship woman on the flats. Her boat is pinned together with iron, and on the Shore iron does not last the season. It goes to rust-lace. You can read through it."

"I heard her kick the hull this morning, and I was here." He knots a cord of root-fibre round a bundle of the pegs. "Treenails. Fallen ghost-oak, the heartwood, dry as last year's leaves. Drive them wet and they swell tight and stay. Willow says we wait to be asked. A boat on the bottom of the sea asks nothing, so take these to her before it gets there."
quests.progress: "Treenails. From the carver? What does he want for them?"
quests.complete:
Ondine turns a treenail over, then another, and for a while says nothing at all. Then she sets one in a split plank and drives it home with the heel of her hand. It goes in with a squeal and sits there as if it had grown. "Wooden nails. My grandfather would have laughed. My grandfather never saw what this coast does to iron."

"Tell the carver..." She stops, and starts again, more carefully. "Tell him I asked. Late. But I asked."

steps.text: Take the treenails to Ondine Varro at the scout's camp on the Salt-Flats.

objectives.text: Bring the treenails to Ondine Varro
objectives.say: "From the wood-folk? For me?" She looks at the bundle as if it might be a trick. "Give it here."

quests.title: Salt in the Reeds
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: glass-frogs in the undergrowth (book3 ch.2) and the Salt-Flats of the western coast (book3 ch.3) are CANON; the Wending, its reeds and the rinsed salt are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: The glass-frogs of the lower Wending have gone quiet from the Reed-bed footbridge down to the sea. Walk the river's reeds for Reed-Song, and ask the glass-ship scout on the flats what her people have been doing at its mouth.
quests.offer:
Reed-Song does not look up from the water. "The mere sings again. Good. Now the river does not." She tips her head toward the north-west, where the Wending slides away to the sea. "The frogs of the lower river have gone quiet, from the reed-bed bridge to the mouth. A whole river of them, all at once. Frogs do nothing all at once unless something makes them."

"Walk the reeds. Look at the roots, not the tops; the tops lie. And there is a woman of the glass ships camped on the flats by the mouth. Flesh-folk notice what flesh-folk do. Ask her."
quests.progress: "Look at the roots. The tops lie."
quests.complete:
Reed-Song hears all of it with her eyes shut, which is how she hears everything. "Salt in the reeds. The mere does not like salt, and the river likes it less." A long pause, the length of a frog's patience. "The tidal pools, she said? Good. The pools are the sea's already. Let the sea have its own salt back."

"Come back in a moon and listen. If they are singing, I will tell you so. If they are not, I will tell you that too."

steps.text: Walk the reeds of the lower Wending, from the Reed-bed footbridge down to the river's mouth.

objectives.text: Look at the reeds under the Reed-bed footbridge
objectives.say: Reeds grow thick round the footbridge piles, and among them not one frog. At the waterline every reed-root is rimmed with something white and gritty. You touch a finger of it to your tongue: salt.

objectives.text: Look at the reeds at the Wending's mouth
objectives.say: At the mouth the reeds stand white to the knee, crusted like a hedge in a hard frost. In the mud of the bank are a dozen hollows the shape of sacks, and a trodden path runs from them through the shallows toward the scout's camp on the flats.

steps.text: Ask the glass-ship scout on the Salt-Flats what her people have been doing at the river's mouth.

objectives.text: Ask Ondine Varro about the salt in the reeds
objectives.say: "Rinsing it." Ondine has the grace to look caught. "Salt off the flats is grey, and Port Caelum pays for white, so the crew rinse the sacks in the river and let the river carry the grey away." She looks toward the mouth, where the reeds are white. "Frogs. Nobody ever tells you about the frogs. Very well: the tidal pools from now on. The sea won't miss a little more salt."

quests.title: What Makes a Briar Hunt
quests.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: the creeping briars and what Alder-Knot finds in one. The cold of the Pale is CANON (book3 ch.2-8); its reaching the Shore this early is PROVISIONAL foreshadowing.
quests.summary: Bring Alder-Knot two briar-heart knots from the creeping briars of the Briar Way or the Fern Hollow, so he can cut one open and see what makes a briar hunt.
quests.offer:
Alder-Knot is whittling, and not looking at what he whittles. "Willow says briars creep. Briars do not hunt. Oak-Bane says a briar on the old way took a fawn. Both of them are older than anything you have ever met, and one of them is wrong."

"In the middle of every creeping briar there is a knot, root and thorn wound round itself, where a briar keeps whatever it has instead of a heart. Bring me two. I will cut one open. The other I will keep shut, in case the first tells me something I do not like."
quests.progress: "Two knots. They are in the thick of the thing, where the thorns are worst. Naturally."
quests.complete:
Alder-Knot sets one knot on his carving-stump and opens it with three careful cuts, like a nut. The outside is green wood, wet and stringy. The middle is grey and dry as ash, and at the very centre sits a grain of something white that does not melt in the warmth of his palm.

"Frost," he says. "In a briar. In summer." He drops the other knot into a jar of resin and stoppers it, and does not look at it again. "Willow is right. Briars do not hunt. Something is hunting with them."

steps.text: Cut briar-heart knots from the creeping briars of the Briar Way or the Fern Hollow.

objectives.say: "Two. Good. Put them on the stump, not in my hand."

quests.title: Light Through Leaves
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: Port Caelum and the Gilded Bay, where the Trade Princes keep their pleasure barges, are CANON (world_bible.md); Ondine's trade in stag hides is GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Bring Ondine Varro three dappled hides from the stags of the Antler Meadow, north of Rootfast, for the Trade Princes of the Gilded Bay.
quests.offer:
Ondine has a ledger open on a crate and is frowning at it the way other people frown at the weather. "When the ship sails she'll have salt in her hold, and salt pays, but it pays like salt. I want one thing aboard that makes a Trade Prince of the Gilded Bay forget to haggle."

"There are stags in a meadow north of the wood-folk's village with hides dappled like sun through leaves. Nobody on the Bay has ever seen one. Bring me three and I'll pay for them as if they were glass. The wood-folk say the herd is too big this year, so even the trees shouldn't sulk."
quests.progress: "Dappled. Not torn. A Trade Prince can find a hole from across a room."
quests.complete: Ondine spreads a hide over the crate and stands back, and the dapple seems to move as the leaves overhead move, as if the light were still on it. "Oh, they'll pay for that." She rolls it up with the others, quickly, the way you cover a good hand of cards. "On the Bay they'll say it came from the edge of the world. For once they'll be right."

steps.text: Take dappled hides from the stags of the Antler Meadow.

objectives.say: "Let me see the dapple. Yes. Oh, yes."

quests.title: The Brother Who Went Listening
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Silent Pilgrims and their brass listening-tubes (book3 ch.5), the Veridian Temple's stair of calcified roots (book3 ch.7) and Oak-Bane are CANON; Brother Wystan is GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Brother Wystan, who came west with Sister Iselle, went to listen at the Veridian Temple and has not come back. Ask Oak-Bane, who keeps the Temple way, and find where Wystan sat.
quests.offer:
Sister Iselle has her brass tube in her lap and is not listening through it. "I did not come to the Shore alone. Brother Wystan came with me. He has the better ear; he always had. When I found the gap where the third note should be, he said the gap was not empty. He said it was leaning. Toward the Temple, and down."

"He went to listen there with a day's bread. A pilgrim can go a long while on a day's bread, but not this long. The Keeper with the staff watches the Temple way. Ask him. And find where Wystan sat. He will have left something. He always leaves something."
quests.progress: "A mark, a bowl, a page. He is tidy in his habits, if in nothing else."
quests.complete:
Sister Iselle studies the circles you copied for her for a long time: three of them, the third filled in so hard the point went through the moss to the wood.

"He heard it." She does not sound glad. "He heard the third note, and he went down to hear it closer, and the roots let him." She lifts her brass tube and points it at the ground, and listens, and lowers it again. "I cannot hear him. That means nothing. The ground is very thick."

steps.text: Ask Oak-Bane on the Temple way whether he saw Brother Wystan.

objectives.say: "The flesh-folk in yellow linen, with the brass ear." Oak-Bane's voice is a branch settling under snow. "He sat under the Ghost-Oaks west of the stair for four days, and did not eat what I left him. Then the roots let him down, and closed behind him. I did not stop him. He asked. He asked very politely."

steps.text: Find where Brother Wystan sat, under the Ghost-Oaks west of the Temple's root-stair.

objectives.say: Between the roots of a Ghost-Oak, a hollow worn to the shape of a sitting man. A wooden bowl, Oak-Bane's food still in it, gone to moss. And scratched deep into the moss of the root, three circles side by side, the third filled in so hard the point went through to the wood. You copy them as best you can.

quests.title: Lanterns for the Laid-Down
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Keepers and the forest's glowing growth are CANON (book3 ch.2, 4, 7); the Keepers' custom of hanging a lantern where one of them went back into the soil is GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Pick three caps of glade-light for Moss-Lantern's grave-lanterns. Then lay the withered Keepers of the Greying down again, and hang the lanterns in the grove's grey heart after dark.
quests.offer:
Moss-Lantern's fingers are busy with rind and resin, making a lantern smaller than any on the trunks. "When one of us goes back into the soil, we hang a lantern where they stood, so the roots know where to look for them. Three of ours went into the Greying to sing. You laid them down. Nobody has hung their lanterns."

"Sap will not burn in that grove; the grey drinks the light out of it. Glade-light will. The Pilgrim showed you how to pick it so it does not remember being picked. Bring me three caps and I will make the lanterns. They must be hung after dark, in the grey heart of the grove. And the grey keeps lifting the dead up again, so you will have to lay them down first."
quests.progress: "Three caps. Gently. Then the dark, and the grey heart."
quests.complete:
Moss-Lantern listens with her hands folded over her middle, as if she were warming them. "Three lights in the grey. Good. The roots will find them now."

"They were not easy kin, those three. Greyheart once argued with the rain for a whole spring." She very nearly smiles. "Go and sit by the Hearth-Tree fire. There are sap-cakes. You will not want one, after that grove. Eat one anyway."

steps.text: Pick glade-light from the glowing caps in the Whispering Glade.
steps.say: The three caps hum against each other in your hand like bees in a jar.

steps.text: Bring the glade-light to Moss-Lantern.

objectives.say: "Hold still." She seats a glowing cap in each little lantern and seals it with resin, and the light steadies, green and patient. "There. Three. Carry them by the cord, not the cup."

steps.text: Lay the withered Keepers of the Greying down again, and hang the lanterns in the grove's grey heart after dark.

objectives.text: Hang the lanterns in the Greying's grey heart, after dark
objectives.say: You hang the three lanterns from a grey branch over the bare heart of the grove. Their light is small and green and does not flicker. Under your feet, very faintly, something in the roots turns toward it, the way a sleeper turns toward a voice.

quests.title: The Quiet in the South Wood
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Void-Touchers in the mists below the ridge, where the grass turns to ash as they pass (book3 ch.2, 4), and glass-frogs (book3 ch.2) are CANON; the walkers straying into the south wood are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: The glass-frogs of the far south wood have stopped singing along a line that runs from Palemist Hollow toward the Mistmere. Find the line for Reed-Song, then follow it back and break what walks it.
quests.offer:
Reed-Song has one hand flat on the water, the way Willow lays hers on a trunk. "Listen south." You listen. "No. Further. Past the ferns, in the big trees." There is nothing to hear. "That is what I mean. A line of nothing, from the cold hollow under the ridge toward my mere. Every frog along it has stopped. Something walks that way, slowly. It is in no hurry, and it is not going to stop."

"Find the line in the south wood. Then find what walks it."
quests.progress: "Still nothing on the line. And it is nearer the mere than it was."
quests.complete:
Reed-Song lifts her hand from the water and listens south for a long time. "There," she says at last. "One frog. A small one, and not very good at it. It will do."

"Ash in the grass, you said. A line of it." She looks at her own long reed-coloured fingers. "Willow says the cold has a hand on it. I did not believe her. I am an old fool, and the mere is older, and the mere believed her first."

steps.text: Find the line of silence in the far south wood.

objectives.text: Find the line of silence in the south wood
objectives.say: Under the giant trees of the far south wood a path of grey runs through the green, a stride wide and straight as a pulled rope, the grass on it gone to ash. On either side the undergrowth is loud with glass-frogs. On it, nothing. It runs east toward the ridge and west toward the Mistmere.

steps.text: Follow the line of ash back toward Palemist Hollow, and break the mist-walkers walking it.

quests.title: A Name in the Fog
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Void-Touchers, who have forgotten their human names (book3 ch.2), and the Silent Pilgrims' masks of polished silver (book3 ch.5) are CANON; Brother Wystan, his fate and the Pilgrims' custom with their masks are GAME-ONLY, and the Pale's fog in the deep before the books is PROVISIONAL.
quests.summary: The fog came up from under the Temple, where Brother Wystan went down. Go into the Root-Mother's Deep, find him among the mist-walkers of the Sap Well, and bring Sister Iselle his mask.
quests.offer:
Sister Iselle has taken off her mask. The face beneath it is younger than her voice, and very tired. "The Keeper told me where the fog comes from. From under the Temple. Where Wystan went to listen."

"You have seen the walkers. People who have forgotten their names." She turns the silver mask over in her hands. "We polish our masks every morning, so that the face behind them is never seen and the voice behind them is never vain. Fog polishes nothing. If he is down there, you will know him by the mask. Let him go, if he is. And bring it back to me. I would not have it walk about without him."
quests.progress: "You will know him by the mask. He will not have polished it."
quests.complete:
Sister Iselle takes the mask in both hands. She rubs at the dent over the mouth with her thumb, as if it might come out. Then she turns it over and reads the name scratched inside, and her shoulders go down slowly, like a sail when the wind drops.

"He wrote it in. In case." Folded in the lining is a page. She reads it, and gives it to you without a word, and puts her own mask back on, and for a long while does not trust her voice.

steps.text: Go down into the Root-Mother's Deep and find Brother Wystan among the mist-walkers of the Sap Well.
steps.say: Among the walkers of the Sap Well one still wears a mask of silver, gone dull, dented over the mouth. When it falls the mask comes away in your hand. Inside, scratched small and careful: WYSTAN.

steps.text: Bring the mask to Sister Iselle.

objectives.text: Bring the mask to Sister Iselle
objectives.say: "Let me see it. Please."

quests.title: What the Wood Remembers
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: trees that remember everything (book3 ch.2) and Willow-Whisper are CANON; giving a lost name to the wood to keep is GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Carry Brother Wystan's mask to Willow-Whisper, so the wood will keep the name the fog took from him. Then listen for it in the Whispering Glade after dark.
quests.offer:
Sister Iselle holds out the dented mask. "The Archive keeps the masks of its dead in a long room in the south, in rows, each with its name. It is a very quiet room. It is a very long way from here."

"The Keepers say the trees remember everything. The fog makes people forget. It seems to me that the trees should have him, then, and not a shelf." She puts the mask in your hands and closes your fingers over it. "Take it to the Voice of the Wood. Ask her to keep his name. Then come and listen with me, after dark. I want to know if they say it right."
quests.progress: "Has she taken it? Then wait for the dark. The glade talks after dark."
quests.complete:
You find Sister Iselle sitting in the glade with her brass tube in her lap, not using it. She has no need to. The leaves are saying it plainly enough.

"They say it the way he did," she says. "With the weight on the wrong half. He was always so pleased with his name." She is quiet a long time. "Thank you. The Archive would have kept him in a row. This is better. This is a great deal better."

steps.text: Take Brother Wystan's mask to Willow-Whisper.
steps.say: Willow-Whisper sets the mask in a fork of her tree, and the bark closes over it slowly, like water over a stone.

objectives.say: "Say his name. Once, and slowly, so the bark can hear it." You say it. "There. Now the wood has him. Go and listen."

steps.text: Listen in the Whispering Glade after dark.

objectives.text: Listen in the Whispering Glade after dark
objectives.say: The leaves move without wind, as they did before, and the sound they make is very nearly a word. It takes you a moment to know it. They are saying his name, over and over, softly, the way you would say the name of someone asleep.

quests.title: Salt Remembers
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Keepers' staves of white salt-wood (book3 ch.2) and salt that drives the unmaking off like water on hot iron (book3 ch.4) are CANON; Oak-Bane's test at the cold heart of Palemist Hollow is GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: The fog drew back from Oak-Bane's staff of salt-wood. Break salt-crust on the Salt-Flats and carry it into the cold heart of Palemist Hollow, past the pale shadows that stand there, to see what salt does to the fog.
quests.offer:
Oak-Bane holds out his staff of white salt-wood, which he has never once let you near before. "I walked to the edge of the cold hollow. Only the edge. The fog came for me the way water comes for a dry root. Then it touched this." He knocks the staff's foot on the stone. "And it drew back. A hand's width. As if it had burned itself."

"The staff is salt-wood. It grows in the salt of the flats. So: salt. Break two cakes of the crust on the flats and carry them to the heart of the hollow, where it is coldest. The shadows that stand there will not like it. Good. See what the fog does, and come and tell me. Do not embroider. I can tell."
quests.progress: "Well? Did it draw back?"
quests.complete:
Oak-Bane hears it all without moving, which for him is a kind of shouting. "It hissed. It drew back. The ground under it remembered being earth, for a breath." He looks at his staff as if it had told him a secret. "Salt remembers what a thing was before. The cold makes things forget. When the one meets the other, the forgetting loses."

"Tell Willow. No. I will tell Willow. She will want to sing about it, and I would rather be there to stop her."

steps.text: Break two cakes of salt-crust on the Salt-Flats.
steps.say: You wrap the two cakes of salt in a broad leaf. Held close they hum, very faintly, like Oak-Bane's staff.

steps.text: Carry the salt into the cold heart of Palemist Hollow, past the pale shadows that stand there.

objectives.text: Scatter the salt on the cold heart of Palemist Hollow
objectives.say: You crumble the salt over the bare grey ground at the hollow's heart. It hisses like water on hot iron and smokes white, and the violet fog draws back from it an arm's length all round. Where the salt lies, for as long as it takes to breathe in and out, the ground is the dark brown of wet earth. Then the grey creeps back.

quests.title: A Heart Still Green
quests.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: Greyheart, Thorn-Hand and the Guest-Tree, and that a Keeper is grown from a heart still green. The Veridian Keepers, beings of living wood and moss (book3 ch.2), are CANON.
quests.summary: Willow-Whisper promised to grow Thorn-Hand anew. A Keeper is grown from a heart that is still green, and the only one left is deep in Greyheart, whom the Greying keeps lifting up. Take it from him and bring it to Oak-Bane to plant.
quests.offer:
"I said we would grow Thorn-Hand a new one." Willow-Whisper's leaves stir. "I did not say how. A Keeper is not planted from a seed. A Keeper is grown from a heart that is still green, and Thorn-Hand's was cold all through. There is nothing of him left to plant."

"But Greyheart, in the Greying. The cold took all of him but the middle. I felt it when you laid him down: one knot of green, deep in, that the grey never reached. The grove keeps lifting him up again, and the green is still there. Take it from him. Two old friends in one sapling. They will argue, but they always did. Bring it to Oak-Bane. Planting in the deep wood is his work."
quests.progress: "Green? In Greyheart? Show me."
quests.complete:
Oak-Bane cups the green heart in both hands like water he does not mean to spill. He kneels, which you have never seen him do, and presses it into the black earth beside his stone, at the head of the Temple way, where the root-stair goes down to the place Thorn-Hand lay.

"Greyheart and Thorn-Hand," he says. "One argued with the rain, and one planted a tree for strangers. Now they will have to share a trunk." Something in the dry crack of his voice might be a laugh. "It will grow crooked. Good. I would not know it otherwise."

steps.text: Take the heart that is still green from Greyheart, in the Greying.
steps.say: Greyheart goes down, and in the split grey heartwood of his chest, deep in, past where the cold glass lay, something is green: a knot of living wood the size of a fist, wet and warm, beating very slowly.

steps.text: Bring the green heart to Oak-Bane on the Temple way.

objectives.text: Bring the green heart to Oak-Bane
objectives.say: "Green. In Greyheart." Oak-Bane's amber eyes burn very bright. "Give it here. Slowly."
